html:
SMTO-WEB-0048 — This request for more research steps no longer matches

GUID: 463a9184-33d6-51f8-bc62-5c099bfed6e5
Slug: research-budget-request-invalid
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • Either SMTO asked for extra research steps in a way that isn't allowed, or a Continue research answer was for a request that's out of date because the task changed. Nothing was approved and no extra lookups happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Refresh the page and look for the newest Continue research prompt in the conversation. An answer only counts for the exact request that is waiting now, not an older one.
  2. Answer it with Allow these additional steps or Don't allow. SMTO only accepts these two choices for a request for more research steps.
  3. If no prompt is showing, let SMTO continue; it will ask again properly if it still needs more steps. The mismatched request was turned down before anything changed, so nothing needs undoing.

What success looks like

  • Your answer is accepted and SMTO either continues researching or finishes with what it has.

If it still fails

  • If your answer to the newest prompt is still refused, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A research budget request used unsupported budget keys or increments outside 1-64, or a user decision did not match the current pending budget request (stale request, operation, intent, contract or decision type).

What this means

  • Budget increments use unsupported keys or non-integer/out-of-range values, or an answer no longer matches the pending request, operation, purpose, intent, contract or decision type. This decision changes no acquisition outcome and does not itself perform external access. Existing user decisions, intent scope and hard bounds remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Budget increments use unsupported keys or non-integer/out-of-range values, or an answer no longer matches the pending request, operation, purpose, intent, contract or decision type.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish malformed increments from a stale or mismatched pending-decision answer.

How to fix it

  • budgets.request() rejects increments whose keys are not in SOFT_LIMITS or whose values are not integers in 1-64; answer_in() raises InputConflict when pending_wait, request_id, operation_id, intent digest or contract digest no longer match, and ValueError when the decision is neither allow nor deny. Answer the current pending authority request with its exact identity; never reuse stale decision IDs or apply a decision to a different request.
  • Correct supported increments, or answer the exact current pending request without reusing stale decision IDs.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use supported bounded increments and the exact matching current pending-decision identity.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid bounded request and its matching current user decision pass the supported authority flow.

What not to do

  • Do not apply a decision to a different budget request or invent a matching request identifier.

Technical notes

  • This decision changes no acquisition outcome and does not itself perform external access. Existing user decisions, intent scope and hard bounds remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
